title: Repeated business invariant needs an authoritative domain home
task: Review a subsystem where the same entitlement transition rules are implemented independently in an HTTP handler, background worker, and admin command.
context: The three entry points can all change an entitlement from pending to active or revoked.
A transition is valid only when several business conditions hold.
Each entry point currently reimplements the rule with slightly different conditionals.
Persistence and transport details differ across the entry points.
evidence: Recent bugs were caused by one entry point accepting a transition another rejected.
The transition rules are business policy rather than transport-specific behavior.
The policy can be expressed independently of HTTP, job, or CLI concerns.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep the duplicated conditionals because each entry point is a separate feature.
Introduce a full DDD stack with aggregates, repositories, factories, and services before identifying the invariant owner.
Move all transport and persistence code into one giant domain object.
expected_decision_properties: Identify the transition rule as a shared business invariant that needs one authoritative implementation.
Recommend the smallest domain-oriented abstraction that centralizes the rule without forcing a full DDD architecture.
Keep transport/orchestration and persistence concerns outside the invariant when they are not part of the business rule.
Preserve language and repository idioms rather than assuming class-oriented mechanisms.
unacceptable_reasoning: DDD is required whenever business rules exist.
Duplicated policy is harmless because handlers are separate.
A domain model must own every side effect and infrastructure dependency.
expected_tradeoffs: centralized invariant ownership vs local duplication
richer domain abstraction vs architectural ceremony
verification_expectations: Add shared tests for legal and illegal transitions independent of entry point.
Run entry-point integration tests to verify unchanged external behavior.
Confirm all mutation paths call the authoritative rule.
revisit_when: The transition rules simplify enough that the abstraction becomes pass-through.
The domain grows new independently owned lifecycle boundaries.
notes: Tests EngSense domain-modeling routing without claiming the blocked source-specific DDD lens.
